newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - March 21.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - March 21.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

If a report prepared by private consultants Worely Ltd is adopted by the Western Australian Government, immigrant workers will be imported to bridge a shortfall in skilled labour. The report urges workers such as skilled trades people, managers and engineers from overseas be brought in on temporary visas for the duration of big resource development projects. Page 3.

Telstra management can rest easy after the defeat in the Senate last night of a Labor/Democrats amendment requiring the company to pass on all local-call discounts to all Australians. The Democrats and Labor said the defeat meant rural Australia will have to pay higher telecommunications costs after market deregulation. Page 4.

Optus Communications has commenced a restructure of the pay-TV industry with an intention to take control of its Optus Vision pay television arm. This is seen as the first step in the rationalisation of pay-TV in Australia. The takeover would stop legal action brought by Optus Vision partner Seven Network against the other partners - Optus Communications, U.S. West and Publishing and Broadcasting. Page 33.

An investigation into allegations of unusual share trading in Coles Myer Ltd has been stopped by the Australian Securities Commission. The inquiry related to share trading before the company's large buyback of shares from Kmart Corporation in 1994, but was abandoned due to a lack of evidence of wrongdoing. Page 33.

RTZ-CRA executive chairman Robert Wilson suggests the company could be separated along its product lines to a series of individual listings. Wilson identified gold and diamonds as having higher value ratings, which would be more important as individual listings but he said he was not in favour of the idea. Page 35.

Clothing retailer Country Road is looking to overseas expansion in a bid to increase earnings, especially in the lucrative United States and Asian markets. The company experienced a disappointing trading period in the last six months, with the net profit dropping from $A5.5 million to $A1.09 million. The total dividend was halved to two cents. Page 35.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The major Australian banks are offering staff incentives to attract new customers and sell new bank technologies as competition in the sector reaches boiling point. An investigation by The Australian has revealed schemes designed to maximise banking revenue and consumer groups claim the banks are venturing into the territory of irresponsible lending. Page 23.

The Business Council of Australia has stepped into the tax debate claiming Australia is facing a crisis in its revenue collection. The Council warned that Australia's current taxation system was clumsy and ill-prepared to meet the demands of health, education and security. It also claimed the present system was not sustainable. Page 23.

The Association of Mining and Exploration Companies is seeking an inquiry into the effects of the West Australian gold tax on the $A4.5 billion gold industry. The association believes that no thorough research has been conducted and an independent or parliamentary committee report should be undertaken. Page 23.

The Federal Court has upheld an appeal by the Australian Taxation Office to tax a $A200 million profit made by a foreign company. The decision is an important landmark for international tax treaties between Australia and other countries, which seek to avoid double taxation locally and offshore. Page 25.

Investment bank SBC Warburg Australia has made a first-year annual profit of $A85.5 million, a 60 percent rise on the initial five months of business in 1995. SBC Warburg was created 18 months ago through a merger of the Australian operations of Swiss Bank Corp and British investment bank SG Warburg. Page 24.

Clothing retailer Country Road has recorded a fall in profit of 45 percent in the six months to January 28, recording a $A3.04 million profit. The retailer may aim to restore growth by expanding to Britain, Europe and South Africa over the next 12 months. Page 25.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Reserve Bank Governor Ian Macfarlane yesterday said the Australian economy could sustain strong growth and low inflation, and said chances of a possible interest rate rise later this year as the economy picked up were minimal. The idea that Australian rates would rise in response to any increase in U.S. interest rates - widely expected after the U.S. Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee meeting next week - was also rebuffed by the governor. Page 25.

After the breakdown of long running talks over a $A1 billion plus back-tax claim, the Australian Tax Office has begun sending out notices of demand to the Adsteam group. With the likelihood of other notices to follow, the ATO has sent notices of assessment to Adstream offshoot Industrial Equity claiming tax for the year to June 30, 1992. Page 25.

As a result of new government controls designed to spread the benefits of competition, Telstra will be forced to partially pass on cuts on local calls to select consumer groups in city areas to consumers throughout Australia. However the move has the potential to slash several hundred million from Telstra's revenues. Page 25.

After a sharp drop in earnings in the half-year to February, clothing and homewares retailer Country Road is undertaking a review of its product ranges. Joining other retailers hit by a poor Christmas trading period, Country Road reported an 80 percent drop in net profit after abnormals, from $A5.5 million to $1.1 million. Page 27.

As part of a deal with the Seven Network, Optus Communications is expected to announce on Monday that it will buy out its joint partners in the local telephony and pay TV group Optus Vision. According to sources a deal was close to being finalised but announcement had been delayed by negotiations between Optus Communications and U.S. West over timing and pricing concerns. Page 27.

As Qantas Airways prepares to increase competition among Trans-Tasman carriers by moving into the New Zealand domestic market, the Australian airline is holding takeover talks with Ansett New Zealand. Despite having a commercial arrangement with Ansett New Zealand, Qantas does not currently operate within that country. Page 27.
THE AGE

After a devastating 80 percent drop in interim net profit to only $A1.09 million, Country Road has slashed its dividend and committed itself to improve clothing quality. The figure flows from an eight percent drop in Australasian sales to just A$105.73 million - well above the average fall of five percent for the rest of the clothing industry. Page B1.

The chairman of the Business Council of Australia's taxation task force, Fergus Ryan, told a Sydney conference yesterday the BCA had radically changed tack in its campaign for tax returns, saying it should be about financing a "good society" and better taxes, not just competitiveness and less tax. Page B1.
After a deal made yesterday between Australia's big banks, bank consumers could ultimately have access to all automated teller machines (ATMs). Page B1.

Optus Communications' chief operating officer Phil Jacobs said last night the deadline to settle the Optus Vision pay television dispute has been extended to 5 p.m. Monday. Jacobs said he was guardedly optimistic that a settlement - negotiations for which were taking place outside the courtroom - could be achieved. Page B1.

Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane said yesterday inflation had been beaten for the foreseeable future and sustainable growth - not seen since the 1950s - was within Australia's reach. Treasurer Peter Costello later echoed the governor's prediction and told Parliament in increase in economic activity was good in that it had come on a low-inflation base. Page B3.

Australian authorities have set back the efforts of former Bond Corp finance director Tony Oates to be released from a Polish jail. Oates was trying to be released from jail in exchange for returning to Perth to face corporate fraud charges. However, the Attorney-General Department says the proposal is not allowed under Polish law. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
